brief: Morgan Stanley sees the equity correction that began months ago entering its final phase, with the S&P 500 catching down toward weaker breadth even as the average stock improves: the equal-weight S&P has outperformed the cap-weighted index and the Russell 2000 by 6% and 4% since September as 10-year yields fell. MS wants either further sentiment-indicator confirmation or the S&P 500 reaching its 7100-7300 downside tactical target before adding risk more aggressively; its year-end base case is 8000. Three clearing events remain. Fed Chair Warsh called financial conditions "tighter" but not "tight," keeping the bar for a dovish pivot high, though a Treasury cash-account drawdown into year-end could ease liquidity. Midterms should help, with large caps historically gaining ~15% over six months, though MS sees a bigger risk in post-election escalation with Iran or new tariffs. Third, Q3 earnings continue favoring quality: free cash flow surprises are driving larger price reactions than EPS surprises, reinforcing MS's preference for durable cash generators -- Industrials remains its top pick among quality cyclicals.
